short: The first major Allied military operation of the Western Desert Campaign, resulting in a stunning defeat of Italian forces.
full:
In December 1940, British and Commonwealth forces launched a five-day raid against Italian positions in western Egypt. Finding Italian defenses surprisingly fragile, the raid was quickly expanded into a full-scale offensive. Over the next two months, the highly mobile Allied force pushed the Italian Tenth Army hundreds of miles across Libya, capturing the vital port of Tobruk and decisively defeating the Italians at Beda Fomm.

The operation resulted in the capture of over one hundred thousand Italian soldiers and massive amounts of equipment, virtually destroying the Italian army in North Africa. However, the advance was halted when Allied troops were diverted to Greece. The spectacular Italian collapse prompted Adolf Hitler to dispatch the Afrika Korps under Erwin Rommel to Libya, dramatically changing the character of the desert war.
